cards.front: Recall a key point about Cinematography
cards.back: Cinematography encompasses all visual choices made with the camera to create meaning and emotion in film.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cinematography
cards.back: Camera shots are defined by distance: extreme long shot establishes setting, long shot shows full body, medium shot frames waist-up, close-up fills the frame with face or object, extreme close-up isolates a tiny detail.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cinematography
cards.back: Camera angles communicate power and status: low angles make subjects appear powerful and dominant, high angles make them seem vulnerable or small, eye-level angles feel neutral and objective.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cinematography
cards.back: Dutch or canted angles create unease, disorientation and psychological instability, commonly used in horror and thriller genres.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cinematography
cards.back: Camera movement includes pans, tilts, tracking shots, dolly shots, crane shots, handheld and steadicam, each producing distinct emotional and narrative effects.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cinematography
cards.back: Tracking and dolly shots follow subjects through space, creating audience immersion and involvement in the on-screen action.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cinematography
cards.back: Handheld camera produces shaky, unstable imagery that conveys immediacy, realism, chaos or documentary-style authenticity.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cinematography
cards.back: Composition uses the rule of thirds, leading lines, depth and symmetry to arrange visual elements within the frame and guide the audience's eye.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cinematography
cards.back: Deep focus keeps foreground and background in sharp focus simultaneously, allowing layered meaning and giving the audience choice about where to look.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cinematography
cards.back: Shallow focus isolates a subject against a blurred background, directing attention and creating intimacy or concealment.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cinematography
cards.back: Lighting creates mood and atmosphere: high-key lighting is bright and even for comedies and safety, low-key lighting creates strong shadows for drama and threat.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Cinematography
cards.back: Three-point lighting uses key, fill and back lights to shape the subject, while practical lighting comes from visible in-scene sources for realism.
